category: URL-to-browser relay (server fetches a direct link, user downloads the stream)

free_tier.stated: 'Grab any file from a link or URL instantly with our fast and easy online downloader. Max. File size: 1 GB.' The page advertises 'Unlimited Downloads - No restrictions on download frequency or usage' and requires no account in the visible flow.
free_tier.notes: The client sends a URL, their server pulls it, and the browser receives the stream. Nothing is stored for later re-download.

per_object_cap.stated: 1 GB per file ('Max. File size: 1 GB').

retention.stated: not applicable in the storage sense: there is a progress screen ('Preparing download... Downloading Secure Server') and no library. Nothing was found that says a fetched file persists.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited Downloads - No restrictions on download frequency or usage'; no byte allowance stated.
egress.free_allowance: no published allowance monthly; 1 GB per file

interface_detail: One web form: paste a direct file URL, press start, watch a progress panel. No API documentation.
tooling: Browser only. A wrapper would need a headless browser because the transfer is streamed through the page.
chaining: It solves the case where a user's own connection cannot reach a host but the relay can: the relay fetches and re-serves over HTTPS. It is a proxy, not storage, so it must be followed immediately by a real download.

limits.value: claimed unlimited ('No restrictions on download frequency or usage'); untested

limits_note: The page also says '100% Secure' and 'End-to-end encryption', which cannot be true of a relay that terminates TLS on both sides; treat the security text as marketing.
binding_note: The 1 GB per-file ceiling is the only hard number: 1 TiB/month is 1024 such files, so frequency is not the wall, the single-file size is.

identity_cost.detail: No login or account appears anywhere in the pasted-URL flow.

reliability_note: A relay is a single point of failure and a single point of visibility: the operator sees every URL and every byte, and the stream dies if the operator's egress is slow. Nothing on the page states uptime or operator identity.
confidence_note: The page and its numbers are read, but no URL was actually pulled through it, so neither the 1 GB ceiling nor the unlimited claim is measured. A single fetch of a small public file would settle both.

evidence.proved: 'Max. File size: 1 GB', 'Unlimited Downloads - No restrictions on download frequency or usage', the progress UI ('Preparing download...') and no account requirement

notes: Answers a narrower question than asked: it will not resolve a Rapidgator page into a direct link, but it will fetch a direct link a user cannot reach. Worth keeping as the last hop.
